subject: Still struggling with annotating different facet plots

messages.author: ab2d30f198bd2360
messages.subject: Still struggling with annotating different facet plots
parts:
Nice package, plan on using it build figures in a large gov't report.

But annotating plots when faceting isn't intuitive yet. For this
example:

examp<-data.frame(X=rnorm(20),Y=rnorm(20),fact=rep(c
("a","b"),each=10))
p<-ggplot(examp,aes(X,Y))+geom_point()+facet_grid(fact~.)+geom_smooth
(method="lm")
p+annotate("text",x=c(0,0),y=c(1,1),label=c
("correlation1","correlation2"))

how do I get a UNIQUE LABEL (e.g., correlation coefficient) into each
plot??

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Still struggling with annotating different facet plots
parts:
Hi Daren,

Create a data frame that indicates where each label should go:

examp <- data.frame(
X=rnorm(20),
Y=rnorm(20),
fact=rep(c("a","b"),each=10)
)

corr <- ddply(examp, "fact", summarise, cor = cor(X, Y))

ggplot(examp,aes(X,Y)) +
geom_point() +
geom_smooth(method="lm") +
geom_text(aes(1, 1, label = format(cor)), data = corr) +
facet_grid(fact~.)

Hadley
